chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan from Abdillah ibn Muskhan from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad said:

I said to him: A slave woman, her master had intercourse with her, then he decided to marry her off. What is the status of her child? He said: The status of the child is such, unless her husband stipulates otherwise. The meaning in this report is one of two things: One is that it came out as Taqiyya (dissimulation), because among the general public there are those who go to the opinion that the child follows the mother in all cases. And the second meaning is that we carry it upon the basis that her husband was married to a slave woman belonging to someone else, for indeed the child would be attached to her, unless the master of the slave man stipulates otherwise.

key_terms.بِمَملُوكِ غَيرِهِ: Belonging to someone else (as a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a child born to a freed slave woman married by her master?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad to clarify the principle of *ilqab* (lineage attachment) for a child born to a slave woman (*umm al-walad*) after her manumission and marriage. The scholar offers two nuanced interpretations: either the ruling reflects *Taqiyya* to harmonize with the Sunni view that the child follows the mother, or it specifies a case where the husband married a slave owned by another master, making the child's lineage contingent on the owner's stipulations.
